2012_037_061912regmtg.paragraph: The Troy School District Board of Education met in regular session on June 19, 2012 at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan, opening with a public hearing on the proposed 2012-13 budget presented by Mark Rajter. The recommended General Fund budget sets revenues at $129,234,265 against expenditures of $132,398,263 — a budgeted deficit of $3,163,998 that carries the ending fund balance to $17,427,023 at June 30, 2013 — on a foundation allowance of $8,805.00 per pupil and a blended count of 12,342.67. The packet also carries the April and May 2012 treasurer's reports, personnel and contract items, four bid awards, and the budget amendment and appropriations resolutions.

## Meeting

Troy School District Board of Education regular meeting, June 19, 2012, 7:00 p.m., Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098; district offices at 4400 Livernois, 248.823.4000. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) and posted at vimeo.com/troyschools. The agenda covers a public hearing on the 2012/2013 proposed budget, a report updating Superintendent goals, a four-item consent agenda, personnel items 8.A–8.F, business items 10.A–10.H, policy first and second readings, and a 2011/2012 School Year in Review slideshow.

## 2012-13 proposed budget

Presented by Mark Rajter. Projected blended K-12 membership is 12,342.67, an increase of 30.29 FTE over 2011/12's 12,312.38, on the 90%/10% September/February blend. The foundation allowance is $8,805.00 per pupil, assuming a permanent $470.00 per-pupil decrease plus one-time offsetting revenues of $116 and $52 per pupil for a net reduction of $302.00. The MPSERS retirement rate rises from 24.46% to 27.37% on October 1, 2012; FICA holds at 7.65%. No budget reductions or revenue enhancements are included. Teachers receive a 0.0% schedule increase and no step increases, with a net increase of 8.0 FTE (7.0 full-day kindergarten, 1.0 science coordinator); TESA takes a 2.00% decrease.

## Taxable value and millage

Homestead taxable value moves from 2,212,203,470 to 2,239,838,800 and non-homestead from 1,350,778,350 to 1,219,073,280, with total taxable value 3,562,981,820 to 3,458,912,080. The appropriations resolution levies 18.0000 mills on non-homestead, 11.5563 mills on commercial personal property, 5.5563 mills on homestead and industrial personal property, and 4.9500 mills on all classes for debt retirement — the debt rate rising from 4.70 mills.

## Meeting and agenda

The Troy School District Board of Education (4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098; 248.823.4000; www.troy.k12.mi.us) met at 7:00 p.m. on June 19, 2012 in the Services Building, 4420 Livernois. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW). The agenda ran: public hearing on the 2012/2013 proposed budget; a report updating Superintendent goals; consent agenda items A–D; personnel items A–F; business items A–H; first and second policy readings; and the 2011/2012 School Year in Review.

## Public hearing — 2012-13 proposed budget

Mark Rajter, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services, presented the PowerPoint and a draft budget book marked DRAFT and paginated "Page X of 37." Homestead taxable value rises from 2,212,203,470 to 2,239,838,800 while non-homestead falls from 1,350,778,350 to 1,219,073,280, taking total taxable value from 3,562,981,820 to 3,458,912,080. The September 2011 count was 12,340.98 and the February 2012 count 12,342.67; the 2012-13 blended student count is 12,342.67, an increase of 30.29 FTE over the 2011/12 K-12 membership of 12,312.38, using the 90%/10% September/February blend adopted in 2011/12. The foundation allowance is $8,805.00 per pupil, reflecting a permanent $470.00 per-pupil decrease offset by one-time revenues of $116 and $52 per pupil for a net reduction of $302.00. No budget reductions or revenue enhancements are built into the budget.

Salary and benefit assumptions: the retirement rate is budgeted to rise from 24.46% to 27.37% on October 1, 2012, with FICA unchanged at 7.65%. MESSA Pak rates are held at fixed district cost for Troy Education Association (TEA) and Troy Educational Secretaries Association (TESA) members under negotiated premium caps; Troy Education Support Personnel Association (TESPA) benefits are likewise fixed. Salary expenditures fall $455,263 from the amended 2011/12 General Fund budget. Teachers receive a 0.0% schedule increase and no step increases, with degree advancement included and a net increase of 8.0 FTE (7.0 full day kindergarten, 1.0 science coordinator). Administrators take 0.00%, TESA a 2.00% decrease, TESPA 0.00%, and non-represented staff 0%.

## General Fund

The General Fund summary shows a budgeted beginning fund balance of $20,591,021 at July 1, 2012, revenues of $129,234,265, expenditures of $132,398,263, a budgeted deficit of $3,163,998, and an ending fund balance of $17,427,023 at June 30, 2013. Revenues by source for 2012-13 are local $38,458,432, state $78,194,219, federal $3,701,311 and interdistrict $7,998,223, totaling $128,352,185; other financing sources add transfers in from Food Service ($140,627), Community Education ($589,100), the Durant Fund ($2,153), Troy Career Center ($100,000) and $50,000 in proceeds from the sale of fixed assets. Kinderplus tuition and facility usage fees are zeroed out of the General Fund. By object, expenditures are salaries $68,792,465, employee benefits $36,547,625, purchased services $14,284,628, repairs and rentals $862,358, supplies and materials $7,386,908, capital outlay $184,843 and other $4,337,083, totaling $132,395,910. By function: basic programs $73,152,528, added needs $15,783,105 and adult/continuing education $578,120 for total instruction of $89,513,753; total support services $42,698,715; community services $122,301. Narrative assumptions state General Fund expenses exceed revenues by $3,178,288 with a June 30, 2013 balance of $11,802,567, a Durant Fund balance of $5,610,166 and a combined total of $17,412,733 — figures the fund statements and forecast worksheet carry instead as $(3,163,998), $11,816,857 and $17,427,023.

Fiscal 2012-13 General Fund grants: Adult Education Civics $20,000; Adult Education Family Literacy $120,000; Career Development Grant $60,238 from Oakland Schools; IDEA-Flowthrough $1,899,776; IDEA-Preschool $62,777; Michigan School Readiness $108,800; CTE Millage $70,080; Title I $802,614; Title II Part A $254,920; Title III English Language Acquisition $528,160. The Troy Career Center receives a $3,210,292 Workforce Investment Act grant tied to the Oakland County Michigan Works! Service Centers.

## Other funds

Food Service: beginning balance $956,684, revenues $3,414,309, expenditures $(3,537,041), deficit $(122,732), ending balance $833,952. Troy Career Center: beginning $510, revenues $3,210,292, expenditures $(3,210,532), ending $270. Community Education: beginning $1,228,795, revenues $2,288,467, expenditures $(2,417,016), ending $1,100,246, broken out by Continuing Education, CARE Co., PAL and TOTS. The new Facility Rentals special revenue fund shows revenues of $181,740, expenditures of $(141,740) and an ending balance of $40,000. Debt Service: beginning balance $(1,825,694), revenues $17,322,173, expenditures $(18,625,531), deficit $(1,303,358), ending balance $(3,129,052); the detail schedule lists property taxes of $17,174,042, principal of $13,055,000, interest of $5,179,000 and total expenditures of $18,480,700. The amortization schedule totals $55,315,000 principal and $16,130,750 interest for the 2004 issue (Fund 304), $48,265,000 and $18,530,750 for the 2006 issue (Fund 306), and $103,580,000 principal, $34,661,500 interest and $138,241,500 overall. The 2004 Capital Projects Fund spends its remaining $185,000 to zero; the Capital Projects Maintenance Fund holds $500,000; the Internal Service Fund shows revenues and expenditures of $116,000 with a flat $25,000 balance.

## Millage, history and forecast

Estimated 2012/13 millage totals 16.5063 homestead and 28.95 non-homestead, built from 6.0000 State Education Tax, a 5.5563 hold-harmless rate and 4.9500 debt; commercial personal property totals 22.5063 and industrial personal property 16.5063. In 1993/94 all taxpayers paid 31.0674 mills for operating purposes. Student headcount was 12,328 in September 2011 with 12,343 projected for September 2012. The ten-year General Fund history lists 2012-13 budgeted revenue of $128,352,184, expenditures of $132,391,409, other financing sources of $875,226, beginning balance $14,980,856 plus Durant $5,610,166, ending balance $17,427,023 and $0 in budget reductions; fund balance as a percentage of expenditures is 13.2%. The multi-year forecast projects ending combined General Fund plus Durant balances of $14,013,300 in 2013/14 and $11,784,886 in 2014/15, retirement rates of 28.37% and 29.37%, and cumulative 2003/04-to-current budget reductions of $43,485,585. A blank Michigan Department of Treasury Form L-4029 (Form 614, Rev. 03-12), the 2012 Tax Rate Request due September 30, 2012 under MCL 211.24e, 211.34 and 211.34d, is attached.

## Superintendent goals and minutes

Dr. Fowler reported on visibility, the Facilities Study presented February 7 and February 14, 2012, data processing cost analysis (eSchoolPlus, FinancePlus, a recommendation due spring 2013), and literacy, mathematics, science and social studies goals under "Troy School District Vision 2013." Consent-agenda minutes cover May 1 (Resolution 12-032 honoring Linda Tackett, Health Care Aide at Baker Middle School, 7-0; Resolution 12-033 Teacher Appreciation Week May 7-11; 12-035 appointing Joseph Duda principal of Larson Middle School), the May 15 special meeting (Sara Ma's Prudential Spirit of Community bronze medal; 2004 Capital Projects bid awards 12-039 Data Strategy $161,305.35, 12-040 Merit $172,230.24, 12-041 Data Strategy $203,539.50, 12-042 Netech $750,876.40 and 12-043 Netech $473,515.00; 12-044 supporting the Oakland Intermediate School District budget under Section 624; 12-045 designating Todd Miletti and supporting Mark Katz, Dr. Theresa Rich and Mr. George Ehlert for the Oakland Schools board), and the May 15 workshop.

Rajter: General Fund total $2,018,968.76, special revenue funds $73,755.62, other funds $140,173.36, total check disbursements $2,232,897.74, ACH debits $34,082.18, outgoing wire transfers $2,957,617.15, total disbursements $5,224,597.07. May 2012: General Fund (101) $1,973,368.40, Grant Fund (120) $3,167.83, Special Education (122) $140,996.46, Food Service (520) $9,908.93, Troy Career Center (529) $24,494.58, Community Education (530) $39,479.49, Building & Site (404, 499) $7,164.00, Student Activity (700, 701) $232,679.94, Memorial Scholarship (750) $16,008.00; total check disbursements $2,447,267.63, ACH debits $28,388.68, wires $1,998,478.94, prior period voids ($1,574.00), total $4,472,561.25. Large single items include MESSA premium checks of $959,846.07 and $954,305.22 and Blue Cross Blue Shield checks of $138,360.58 and $137,815.44.

## Personnel

Probationary contracts for 2012-2013 to Jessica Bronsteen (3rd grade, Troy Union), Stacie Getty (3rd grade, Bemis), Jaime Lindstrom (2nd grade, Schroeder), Allison Mason (speech pathologist), Brad Sassack (2nd grade, Wattles) and Zaklina Zavich (4th grade, Wattles). William Turner, hired from Utica Community Schools in June 2005, receives a two-year probationary contract as Assistant Principal, Athens High School, beginning July 1, 2012. Jennifer Gebbie resigns as Assistant Principal, Baker Middle School effective July 1, 2012 (hired June 20, 2005). Dr. Barbara A. Fowler's contract runs through June 30, 2015. Assistant superintendents Dr. Richard Machesky, Jan Keeling, Mark Rajter and Jasen Witt, and thirty named administrators including Mark Dziatczak (Troy High) and Lara Dixon (Athens High), are extended to June 30, 2014.

## Business items

First Student's contract, originally approved April 21, 2009, is extended July 1, 2012 through June 30, 2014 with a 1.5% COLA in fiscal 2013 and 1% in fiscal 2014 rather than the 3.5% 2012 CPI; buses remain 100% district-owned and First Student installs digital cameras at its own cost. Routes fell from 70 in 2010 to 57 in 2012. Enviro-Clean, approved May 19, 2009 with grounds added November 17, 2009, holds 2009-10 pricing and staffing through June 2014. Bid #9733 (opened June 1, 2012, eleven invited, two responses) awards beverage vending to Coca-Cola for 7/1/2012–6/30/2015 with estimated revenue of $117,545. Bid #9734 (opened May 22, 2012, nine invited, two responses) awards snack vending to VendTek at $49,326. Bid #9736 (opened May 31, 2012) awards two-way radios to Cynergy Wireless Products, Inc. at $20,867.25. Bid #9737 awards Troy High and Athens High fencing to Nationwide Construction Group at $40,153.00 against American Fencing's $53,062.00, one bid having been disqualified for missing the mandatory pre-bid meeting. Purchasing Supervisor Sara L. Konieczka (1140 Rankin, Troy, MI 48083) prepared the bid memoranda.

## Budget resolutions and policies

The 2011-12 budget amendment appropriates $130,776,311 for the General Fund, $8,785,651 for special revenue funds, $18,652,488 for debt service, $4,357,340 for capital projects and $116,000 for the internal service fund, with the General Fund ending balance amended to $20,591,023. The 2012-2013 appropriations resolution appropriates $132,398,263 (General Fund), $9,306,329 (special revenue), $18,480,700 (debt service), $185,000 (capital projects) and $116,000 (internal service), and levies 18.0000 mills on non-homestead, 11.5563 on commercial personal, 5.5563 on homestead and industrial personal, and 4.95 mills on all classes for debt retirement. First readings covered policies J-2013 Sexting and K-1601 Trademarks, Service Marks and Trade Names; second readings and adoption covered B-1302 Agendas for Regular Meetings, C-1501 E-mail Retention, G-1006 Placement of Teachers, G-1401 Political Activities, J-3203 Children's Internet Protection Act Policy, K-1303 Commercial Advertising and K-1401 Solicitations on School Property.
